t: You're looking at the Natural History Museum, one of three great museums on Exhibition Road in South Kensington, though its main front faces Cromwell Road. Inside is a vast range of specimens from across natural history. Two men shaped it. Richard Owen, the biologist and palaeontologist, is credited with founding it, and he was known for his remarkable gift for interpreting fossils. The architect Alfred Waterhouse designed the building. He worked mostly in Gothic Revival style, and this is one of the two designs he's best known for, alongside Manchester Town Hall.
